newMessages.content: Task: Explain in three sentences, for a ten-year-old, why the sky is blue.

content.text: Sunlight might look white, but it is actually made up of all the colors of the rainbow. When this light hits the Earth's atmosphere, it bumps into tiny gas molecules and scatters in every direction. Because blue light travels in shorter, smaller waves, it gets scattered much more than the other colors, making the sky look blue to our eyes.

about.description:
A researcher collects the facts and a writer turns them into a short explanation.

**What it teaches**

How a chain passes work along: each agent gets the text of the one before it.

**What to watch**

What the writer received from the researcher, and what it changed.

Read more: [Sequential chain](#/learn/sequential-chain)
